cards.title: Adapt
cards.text:
- Borrow the structure of a genre from another field (sports commentary, safety briefing, auction, weather forecast) and fill it with the brief's content.
- Adapt a solution nature uses for the same problem (camouflage, migration, molting).
- Adapt how a child, a machine or a foreigner would misunderstand the situation, and make the misunderstanding the point.

cards.title: Eliminate
cards.text:
- Remove the element everyone considers essential (the hero, the product shot, the chorus, the word "love") and build around the hole.
- Remove all but one sense (only sounds, only smells).
- Cut the explanation: start after the event, end before the resolution.

cards.title: Pre-empt the objection (Preliminary anti-action)
cards.text: Open with the audience's strongest objection or cynicism and build on top of it, instead of hoping they won't think it.

cards.title: Split it (Segmentation)
cards.text: Break the piece, the hero or the message into independent parts that work alone and add up differently (a story told in separate receipts; a hook made of three overheard fragments).

cards.title: Make one part different (Local quality)
cards.text: Give one part of a uniform structure a different rule: one verse in another tense, one frame in colour, one line spoken by someone else.

cards.title: What does the audience do at 7 a.m.?
cards.text: Ignore the topic; observe the audience's most routine moment, then connect it back.

cards.title: Last line first
cards.text: Write the final moment first and refuse to explain how we got there.

cards.title: Withhold the payoff
cards.text: Promise something and deliberately never deliver it; make the absence the payoff.

cards.title: One room
cards.text: Everything happens in one small, specific room. No flashbacks outside it.

cards.title: Borrowed rhythm
cards.text: The rhythm or structure is copied from a non-artistic sequence (a phone number, a countdown, a bus route, a recipe's steps).

branches.label: Counter-trend and white space, tail-only verbalized sampling

cards.title: Turn harm into benefit (Blessing in disguise)
cards.text: Take the brief's biggest negative (the product's flaw, the audience's bad habit, the topic's taboo) and make it the hook.

cards.title: Make one thing impossible
cards.text: Allow exactly one impossible element and keep everything else painfully realistic.

branches.label: Outsider: conceptual blending with a foreign domain

cards.title: Cave diving
cards.text: Line laying, the rule of thirds for air, silt-out (zero visibility), the restriction, always know the way back.

cards.title: Tax filing
cards.text: Deadlines, deductions, receipts kept in a shoebox, the audit lottery, amended returns, dependants, carry-forward of losses.
